questions.question: Find the mean proportional of 36 and 100.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mean proportional between any two numbers a and b is given directly by the square root of their product.

⇒ Mean proportional = √(a × b)

⇒ Mean proportional = √(36 × 100)

⇒ Mean proportional = 6 × 10 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The two given numbers are 36 and 100.

**Formula Used:**

If x is the mean proportional between a and b, then a : x :: x : b, which implies the product of extremes equals the product of means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4999f36875c51053743a3c9640e73eba45018f32a3b5bfef153b76c117c1725.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the mean proportional be x.

⇒ 36 : x = x : 100

⇒ x × x = 36 × 100

⇒ x² = 3600

⇒ x = √3600

⇒ x = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

For any two numbers a and b, the mean proportional is their geometric mean, calculated as √(a × b).

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c satisfies a : b :: b : c, which results in the formula c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d satisfies a : b :: c : d, yielding the formula d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, the resultant ratio is called a compound ratio. For ratios a:b and c:d, it is (a × c) : (b × d).

questions.solution:

Ratio of the three numbers = 3 : 5 : 8

Let the numbers be 3x, 5x, and 8x.

Sum of the largest and the smallest number = 8800.

**Calculations:**

Smallest number = 3x

Smallest number = 3x = 3 × 800 = 2400

Difference = Largest number - Smallest number

questions.question: The average weight of eleven players' state-level cricket team is 141 kg. When the coach is added then the average weight increases to 1 kg. What is the weight of the coach? (in kg)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of 11 players = 141 kg

Average weight of (11 players + coach) = 142 kg

Total member of team = 11 + 1 = 12

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations/Total number of observations

**Calculation:**

Average weight of 11 players = Sum of weight of 11 players/11

⇒ 141 = Sum of weight of 11 players/11

⇒ Sum of weight of 11 players = 141 × 11 = 1551 kg

Average weight of (11 players + coach) = Sum of weight of all members/12

⇒ 142 = Sum of weight of all members/12

⇒ Sum of weight of all members = 142 × 12 = 1704 kg

Weight of coach = Sum of weight of all members - Sum of weight of 11 players

⇒ Weight of coach = 1704 - 1551 = 153 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 153 kg.**

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 60%, 30% and 20% in three successive months, but increases by 60% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The initial price of fuel = 100 units

Price decreases by 60% in the first month

Price decreases by 30% in the second month

Price decreases by 20% in the third month

Price increases by 60% in the fourth month

**Formula Used:**

Final Price = Initial Price × (1 - Decrease%)ⁿ × (1 + Increase%)

**Calculation:**

Initial Price = 100 units

First month: 100 × (1 - 60/100)

⇒ 100 × 0.4 = 40 units

Second month: 40 × (1 - 30/100)

⇒ 40 × 0.7 = 28 units

Third month: 28 × (1 - 20/100)

⇒ 28 × 0.8 = 22.4 units

Fourth month: 22.4 × (1 + 60/100)

⇒ 22.4 × 1.6 = 35.84 units

Percentage change = [(Final Price - Initial Price) / Initial Price] × 100

Percentage change = [(35.84 - 100) / 100] × 100

Percentage change = -64.16%

**The price of fuel decreases by 64.16% in the fourth month as compared to its original price.**

questions.question: A cylindrical hole with the radius of its base given as 3.5 cm is made in a solid cube each of whose edge is 14 cm. Find the total surface area (in cm²) of the cube with the hole. [Use π = (22)/(7)]

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a hole is drilled completely through a solid, the net Total Surface Area (TSA) is:

Net TSA = (TSA of Cube) − (2 × Base Area of Hole) + (Curved Surface Area of Hole)

Net TSA = 6a² − 2πr² + 2πrh

Net TSA = 6 × 14² − 2 × (22/7) × (3.5)² + 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 14

Net TSA = 1176 − 77 + 308 = 1407 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1407 cm².**

⇒ Edge of the solid cube (a) = 14 cm

⇒ Radius of the cylindrical hole (r) = 3.5 cm

⇒ Height of the cylindrical hole (h) = Edge of cube = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Surface Area = (TSA of solid cube) − (2 × Area of circular bases of hole) + (CSA of cylindrical hole)

⇒ TSA = 6a² − 2πr² + 2πrh

**Calculations:**

⇒ TSA of cube = 6 × 14 × 14 = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm²

⇒ Area of 2 circular bases = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 = 77 cm²

⇒ CSA of cylindrical hole = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 14 = 308 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 1176 − 77 + 308 = 1407 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1407 cm².**

When a hole is drilled completely through a solid, the flat surface area corresponding to the base cuts is lost, but the newly created inner curved surface is exposed and must be added to the total area.

questions.question: A person drove at 39 kmph for 3.5 hours, then increased his speed by 9 kmph, and reached the destination in another hour. Find the average speed (in kmph) of the person during the entire journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person drove at 39 kmph for 3.5 hours, then increased his speed by 9 kmph, and reached the destination in another hour.

**Formula used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

**Calculation:**

Distance₁ = Speed₁ × Time₁

⇒ Distance₁ = 39 kmph × 3.5 hours = 136.5 km

Distance₂ = Speed₂ × Time₂

⇒ Distance₂ = (39 kmph + 9 kmph) × 1 hour = 48 km

Total Distance = Distance₁ + Distance₂

⇒ Total Distance = 136.5 km + 48 km = 184.5 km

Total Time = Time₁ + Time₂

⇒ Total Time = 3.5 hours + 1 hour = 4.5 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 184.5 km / 4.5 hours = 41 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: The shopkeeper added 40% of the cost price as mark up and then he gives a discount of same 40% on the marked price for a sale, then what will be the overall proﬁt or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mark up = 40% of cost price (CP).

Discount = 40% on marked price (MP).

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = Cost Price (CP) + Mark Up

Discounted Price = Marked Price - Discount

Profit or Loss% = ((Selling Price (SP) - Cost Price (CP)) / CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price (CP) = 100 units.

⇒ Mark up = 40% of 100 = 40 units.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + Mark Up = 100 + 40 = 140 units.

⇒ Discount = 40% of 140 = 56 units.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount = 140 - 56 = 84 units.

⇒ Profit or Loss = SP - CP = 84 - 100 = -16 units.

⇒ Profit or Loss% = ((-16) / 100) × 100 = -16%

**∴ The overall percentage is 16% loss.**

questions.question:
Simplify the following expression.

120 ÷ 15 of 4 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of {4 × 2 - (8 - 11)}]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

1. Solve 'of' and Brackets: 15 of 4 = 60 and {4 × 2 − (−3)} = 11.

2. Substitute: 120 ÷ 60 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of 11].

3. Square bracket: [11 × 4 ÷ 44] = [44 ÷ 44] = 1.

4. Total: 2 + 1 = 3.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: 120 ÷ 15 of 4 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of {4 × 2 − (8 − 11)}]

Formula Used: VBODMAS rule (Vinculum, Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 120 ÷ (15 × 4) + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of {8 − (−3)}]

⇒ 120 ÷ 60 + [11 × 4 ÷ 4 of 11]

⇒ 2 + [11 × 4 ÷ 44]

⇒ 2 + [44 ÷ 44]

⇒ 2 + 1

⇒ 3

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It specifies the order of operations: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. Operations are performed from left to right for same-priority levels.

Precedence of 'Of'

The 'Of' operator represents multiplication but carries a higher priority than Division (÷) and standard Multiplication (×).

Bracket Hierarchy

Mathematical expressions are simplified by solving brackets in the specific sequence: Parentheses ( ) → Curly Braces { } → Square Brackets [ ].</p

questions.question: What is the fourth proportional of 3sqrt5, 5sqrt8 and 3sqrt10?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Fourth Proportional (d) = (Second term × Third term) ÷ First term

d = (5√8 × 3√10) ÷ 3√5

d = (5 × 2√2 × 3 × √2 × √5) ÷ (3√5)

d = 5 × 2 × 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

First term (a) = 3√5

Second term (b) = 5√8 = 5 × 2√2 = 10√2

Third term (c) = 3√10

**Formula Used:**

If a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then a/b = c/d ⇒ d = (b × c) / a

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the fourth proportional be d.

⇒ 3√5 / 5√8 = 3√10 / d

⇒ d = (5√8 × 3√10) / 3√5

⇒ d = (10√2 × 3 × √2 × √5) / 3√5

⇒ d = (30 × 2 × √5) / 3√5

⇒ d = 60 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

questions.question: Aarav can do a piece of work alone in 6 days and Babita can do it alone in 8 days. Aarav and Babita undertook to do it for ₹2,400. With the help of Chaitanya, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to Babita?

Total ratio = 4 + 3 + 1 = 8

**∴ The amount to be paid to Babita = ₹900**

questions.question: Which two kings fought in the Battle of Hydaspes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander and Porus**__.

__
 
• **In 326 BC, Alexander the Great** faced **King Porus in the Battle of the Hydaspes**, also known as the **Battle of Jhelum**.
 
• It took place on the banks of the** Jhelum River** (called as Hydaspes by the ancient Greeks) in the **Punjab area **of India (modern-day Punjab, Pakistan).
 
• The conflict ended with a Greek triumph and Porus' capitulation.
 
• Large swaths of Punjab were integrated into the Alexandrian Empire, and Alexander reinstalled the vanquished and dethroned Porus as a subordinate ruler.
 
• One of Alexander's "masterpieces" was his choice to cross the monsoon-swollen river despite intense Indian monitoring in order to catch Porus' army off-guard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alexander III of Macedon**, also known as** Alexander the Great,** was the monarch of Macedon in ancient Greece.
 
• At the age of 20, he succeeded his father Philip II to the throne in 336 BC and spent the majority of his reign executing a lengthy military campaign across Western Asia and Northeastern Africa.
 
• He had built one of the biggest empires in history by the age of thirty, ranging from Greece to northwestern India.
 
• **Porus** was an ancient Indian king whose kingdom stretched between the Hydaspes (Jhelum River) and the Acesines (Chenab River) in the Punjab area of India.

• the euro,

• the Japanese yen, and
 
• the British pound sterling.

• The SDR was created as a supplementary international reserve asset in the context of the Bretton Woods fixed exchange rate system.
 
• The collapse of the Bretton Woods system in 1973 and the shift of major currencies to floating exchange rate regimes lessened the reliance on the SDR as a global reserve asset.
